_comment: BUG-002 investigation, follow-up to step 5 (bug-reports/BUG-002-...md): identical wiring/profile to single_channel_bidirectional_600 (one bidirectional motor, channel 1, held at throttle 100) - the configuration that has NEVER reproduced BUG-002 - except core1_interval_us=250 pads Core 1's sleep, to test whether a slower command-loop tick alone (no second motor at all) can trigger it. RESULT (2026-09-27, session captures/2026-09-27_14-15-34): passed cleanly, 100% CRC-valid, real spin (median 21,246 eRPM) - and its measured average tick (~927us, from captures-published/duration) was SLOWER than the two-bidirectional-motor step-5 run's (~753us), which failed. Tick period alone is therefore ruled out as BUG-002's trigger - see BUG-002's report for the full reasoning. The ADR-002 figures (~175us one-motor / ~366us two-motor) this scenario's padding target was originally based on do not hold for today's code and should not be reused without re-measuring. Kept as a regression/reference scenario for that negative result, not as an active lead.
